_comment: Who Knows the Retiree Best? Twelve light, personal questions about the retiree that coworkers, friends or family answer on their own sheets, then compare against the retiree's real answers. The service never knows or invents an answer: it writes questions only, each one a guess someone who knows the retiree could make. Variety is structural: every question gets its own brief -- a topic, one of its facets and a question shape -- sampled by seed, twelve distinct topics per set (audience-weighted, group-capped, always one about retirement plans), plus spares for the gates on both sides. Questions refer to the retiree only as they/their/them, never address the player, and never touch health, age, money, politics, religion, relationships, private data or anything embarrassing. qualifierWords, phrases and synonyms fold a question to its underlying detail so 'first job' and 'where they worked first' are one question. Brands are the Bucket List's own list (bucket-list/prompt.json).

locale.nativeLine: - Write in clear, warm, natural English that reads well in both British and American homes.
locale.otherLine: - Write every question in language locale '{locale}', natural for that language, keeping each one short and clear.

mixed.label: anyone who knows them -- friends, family and coworkers alike
mixed.line: Players are a mix of friends, family and coworkers, so most questions should be answerable by anyone who knows the retiree reasonably well.

work.label: coworkers
work.line: Players are coworkers, so lean on what colleagues see: routines, workplace habits and what the retiree is known for, alongside a little of their life outside work.

family.label: friends and family
family.line: Players are friends and family, so ask about life, tastes, habits and plans rather than office routines.

shapes.past: about something from their past: what they did, had or chose back then
shapes.habit: about what they usually or always do: a routine or habit people have noticed
shapes.choice: offering two or three named options and asking which one they would pick; the answer is one of the options
shapes.number: asking for a number, a time of day or a count someone could guess (never an age, a price or a salary)
shapes.prediction: asking what they would most likely do in one specific situation
shapes.known-for: about something they are known for: something they say, do or are the go-to person for
shapes.top-pick: asking for the one specific thing they would pick, order, bring or choose
